result.summary: Across two observed 5-second cycles, the workstation task consists of a linear transfer of a single red block across two sequential zones separated by a center boundary line. Because the motion follows a fixed, repeatable linear path with a simple geometric part well within the payload and reach limits of standard 6-axis cobots like the UR5e or Franka FR3, both steps are strong candidates for full automation using a standard two-finger parallel gripper.

steps.name: Transfer red block across left zone

reasons.text: The red block moves along a straight, unobstructed horizontal trajectory toward the center boundary line, which a 6-axis cobot with a parallel gripper can easily execute.
The block maintains a consistent orientation and linear path across the left workspace with no tactile judgement required.

verifier.note: The step boundaries and automate verdict match what is observed across cam0, cam1, and cam2 once camera offsets are applied.

steps.name: Transfer red block across right zone

reasons.text: After crossing the center boundary, the red block continues along the same predictable linear path through the right zone.
Multi-view confirmation shows the part remains rigid and follows a repeatable trajectory to the end of the stroke without complex manipulation.

verifier.note: The step boundaries and automate verdict match what is observed across cam0, cam1, and cam2 once camera offsets are applied.

robot.why: Needed payload 1.15 kg: the heaviest of the parts in the automatable steps is red block at about 150 g plus a 1 kg allowance for the gripper and fingers, assuming the rated payload is at the tool flange and excludes the gripper. Needed reach 504 mm: the farthest pick or place of the automatable steps from the proposed base, kept within 85% of the rated reach; the layout is estimated from video, so treat it as approximate. xArm 6 (5 kg, 700 mm) is the smallest arm in the catalogue that passes every check, with 3.85 kg of payload margin; also adequate: UR5e, Franka FR3, Doosan M0609, UR10e. Not proposed: UR3e (reach short by 4 mm).
robot.gripper: two-finger parallel gripper (Robotiq 2F-85 class), 1 kg allowance
robot.reach_basis: layout estimated from video (Argon call C)

robot_base.rule: on the bench's back edge (across from the operator) or at either end, at the position that minimises the farthest pick or place of the automate and needs_fixture steps

layout.reach_rule: farthest pick or place of the automate and needs_fixture steps from the proposed base, divided by 0.85 so it sits within 85% of the rated reach
layout.notes: Scale is anchored strictly by the 50 mm red block width, which spans roughly 1/16th of the frame width, giving a 0.80 m wide by 0.45 m deep workspace. The video is a synthetic 2D animation with no operator or physical fixtures visible, so y-depth and operator stance are estimated at the center.

cycle_estimate.method: Robot time = the operator's time on the automate steps x 1.3, a conservative factor for a cobot moving at collaborative speed; no robot motion was planned or simulated. Side by side = the longer of the robot's time and the operator's remaining time, the operator keeping the seconds no step covers.
